subject: MAP + Benchmark plan & close timeline — PulseGuard POC
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@pulseguard.io>, Samir Kohli <samir.k@pulseguard.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + Benchmark plan & close timeline — PulseGuard POC

Hi Elena & Samir,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a concise benchmarking plan so we can validate TTFT + streaming latency for chat during the POC and align on a close timeline. High-level items included in the MAP:

- Goals: validate p50/p95/p99 TTFT and streaming per-token latency for 2 prompt lengths (50 tokens, 256 tokens), concurrency profile, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
- POC window: 2027-05-10 → 2027-05-14 (formal close/decision: 2027-05-17)
- Success criteria: p95 TTFT <= 500ms for 50-token prompts at 8 concurrent streams; model quality delta within agreed eval set.

Benchmark plan (summary):
1) Model variants: Redwood-Open-7B (int8), Redwood-Open-13B (int8) — quick compare.
2) Environments: hosted (us-west) and dedicated sandbox (customer VPC) — will route tests to hosted first.
3) Test matrix: prompt lengths 50 / 256 tokens × concurrency [1, 4, 8, 16] × stream mode ON (token-by-token)
4) Metrics captured: TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming per-token latency (first 8 tokens vs steady-state), p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec throughput, and error rates/timeouts.
5) Run cadence: smoke runs 5/10 morning, full runs 5/10–5/12, extended high-concurrency stress 5/13, analysis and deck 5/14.

Quick asks from our side:
- Please confirm the two prompt-lengths above match your worst-case user flows (short chat vs long assistant reply).
- Approve running a 32-concurrency burst on 5/13 to simulate peak night traffic (we will throttle if you want).

Attachments: PulseGuard_MAP_Q22027.xlsx (MAP + milestone tracker), streaming-bench-plan.md (detailed commands & k6 scripts).

I'll book a 30-min sync for Tuesday 5/11 to go over the first smoke-run results.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Dylan@redwood.inference

Thanks Dylan — attached looks good and the timeline is reasonable. A few clarifications from our side before you run the full matrix: 

- Confirmed prompt lengths: 50 tokens (quick guidance message) and 256 tokens (multi-paragraph system-generated reply). Good call.
- Please capture p99 for TTFT and streaming tail (we're sensitive to worst-case tail latency).
- Add a test for average response length of ~120 tokens (our modal reply) so we have a mid-point datapoint.
- We'd like the 8-concurrency baseline. 32-concurrency burst is useful but please provide an opt-in window so we can alert our SRE.

Also: can you include a rough cost delta estimate for Redwood-Open-7B vs Redwood-Open-13B at the throughput you measure? We'll use that in the procurement evaluation.

Appreciate it — look forward to seeing the smoke-run.

Elena
Head of Product | PulseGuard

Elena — quick update from the smoke run I executed this morning (hosted us-west, Redwood-Open-7B int8). I attached a CSV with raw samples and aggregated percentiles. Summary below.

Test matrix run: 50-token / 120-token / 256-token prompts × concurrency [1, 4, 8] (streaming ON). Sample size: ~1,000 requests per cell.

Key results (Redwood-Open-7B, hosted):
- 50 tokens @ concurrency=1: TTFT p50=120ms, p95=260ms, p99=410ms; streaming per-token p50=10ms, p95=22ms, p99=45ms.
- 50 tokens @ concurrency=8: TTFT p50=170ms, p95=420ms, p99=810ms; streaming per-token p50=14ms, p95=35ms, p99=90ms.
- 120 tokens @ concurrency=8: TTFT p50=190ms, p95=480ms, p99=930ms; steady-state per-token p95 ~30ms.
- 256 tokens @ concurrency=8: TTFT p50=220ms, p95=560ms, p99=1,300ms; first 8 tokens show higher variance (p95 ~55ms).

Preliminary notes:
- P95 TTFT at concurrency 8 for 50-token prompts is borderline vs your target of 500ms — we hit ~420ms which meets goal; p99 spikes especially for longer responses (256 tokens).
- Streaming per-token latency is very stable after first 6 tokens; first-token and early-token overhead is the main driver of TTFT.
- Failure modes seen: ~0.2% timeouts at concurrency 8 for the 256-token runs (we logged and attached traces).

Attachments: streaming-bench-results.csv (aggregated percentiles), pulseguard-quick-run.csv (raw samples), smoke-run-traces.zip (traces)

Next steps I propose:
1) Full matrix 5/10–5/12 for Redwood-Open-7B and Redwood-Open-13B (we'll include 16-concurrency cell).
2) High-concurrency burst (32) on 5/13 as requested — we'll notify your SRE window.
3) Deliver a short results deck (pptx) and a cost/throughput appendix by 5/14.

Let me know if you want that 32-concurrency cell removed or shifted.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.inference

Also: we'll need the final results deck to include a short slide showing the MAP milestones and acceptance sign-off to move to Dedicated.
